data.name: Sahasrani
data.gender_notes: Sahasrani is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Sahasra', meaning 'thousand'. Often associated with the Goddess Durga, signifying a thousand flames or radiances. The name Sahasrani carries the meaning “Thousand Flames” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Sahasrani usually hope their child will grow to embody thousand flames and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizing the infinite power and divine light within.
data.etymology: Sahasrani belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Thousand Flames.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sahasrani total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Sahasrani' carries a deep cultural significance in Hindu mythology, particularly with the reverence of Goddess Durga. 'Sahasrani' can be interpreted as one who possesses a thousand fiery eyes, symbolizing an all-seeing nature and divine protection. In festivals like Durga Puja, devotees offer their deepest respects to the Goddess by chanting her thousand names.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name 'Sahasrani' holds profoundDEEP resonance with the inner flames that light the spiritual journey of the soul. The inner fire, believed to represent various emotions and instincts, is brought under the control of the highest self. When viewed through this lens, the name 'Sahasrani' signifies the mastery of one's emotions and instincts, leading to spiritual progress and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sahasrani signifies one who possesses a thousand hearts, embodying boundless compassion and selfless love towards all beings. This name is a reminder to nurture compassion and serve others with an open heart.

vedic_reference.note: Not directly from Vedas or Upanishads

historical_references.reference: Sahasrani was the name of a great soldier in the army of the Hindu king, Harshavardhana (600-647 CE). He is known for leading the successful siege of the fortress of Thanjavur in South India.
Sahasrani was also the name of a Jain Tirthankara who lived around the 12th century BCE. He is considered to have achieved enlightenment through deep penance and introspection.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Sahasrani' in Hinduism is often associated with a thousand blessings or auspiciousness. In modern contexts, this name is popularly used in various spheres such as astrology, spirituality, and wellness. On social media platforms like Instagram and Twitter, users often post pictures or write about their personal experiences related to Sahasrani mantra or astrological readings. Blogs and websites provide in-depth knowledge and resources on the significance of Sahasrani in Hinduism, its connection with various deities, and its contemporary usage in various practices. The name is also used in the context of wellness practices, where it is believed to bring positive energy and blessings.
